column1: L2 turns beliefs about the world into what a MWh, a kW of peak, or a MW of aFRR capacity is worth in euros, expressed as linearizable primitives rather than prices.
L2's input is the BeliefSnapshot plus the lagged StateSnapshot, and its output is the ValuationBundle.
L2 is a total function with no I/O, no clock, no state and no randomness.
Views are independent: a view may not read another view's output, may not share mutable state, and may not know that another view exists.
Composition is the composer's job alone.
View independence is what makes each view a small, individually testable pure function of a recorded C1 payload.
A valuation view exposes an Id, a PublishedSchema, its ClaimedEffects, and an Evaluate over the belief snapshot, the state snapshot and its config.
PublishedSchema is declared as data and Evaluate's output is validated against it, so a view that emits a field it did not declare fails.
The closed published field table is enforced rather than documented.
PeakView prices the marginal kW of grid peak under whichever tariff regimes are active.
PeakView emits one EpigraphTerm per active regime.
PeakView's slot set is all slots for AnnualLeistungspreis and HLZF slots only for AtypicalHlzf, expressed through EpigraphTerm.overSlots, which is why that field is a slot set rather than a range.
PeakView's floor is realisedPeak from L0, adjusted upward for the unsettled gap using the engine's own modelled trajectory.
The peak level PeakView uses is an empirical CVaR tail mean over the joint ensemble rather than the mean forecast.
The CVaR peak level is the weighted mean of the worst (1−α) mass of the per-scenario maximum POI power over the reduced ensemble with its weights.
A risk-averse peak level is the correct treatment because the peak charge is a max-of-a-max, so the mean forecast systematically understates it by Jensen's inequality in the unhelpful direction.
PeakView's prorationFactor scales the in-horizon charge and the remainder is priced by V.
Getting proration wrong is the most common way to make the engine pathologically peak-averse.
Poor load quality adds peakSafetyMarginKw to PeakView's floor rather than changing behaviour.
OppCostView emits a LinearTerm for cycle and throughput cost per kWh from the degradation model, BoundTerms for power and POI limits, and the PwlTerm carrying V(SOC).
OppCostView does not emit λ_SOC, which is an output of the Planner obtained as the subgradient of V at the optimum and reported in PlanResult for diagnostics only.
Degradation cost is charged once, in OppCostView, on BatteryThroughput.
If the value function was fitted on net-of-degradation cashflows, the ownership check catches the double count.
AfrrCapacityView emits a BoundTerm for the MW envelope from prequalification and asset limits and a concave maximising PwlTerm for the expected value of the capacity bid curve.
Concavity of the capacity curve arises from the clearing model: offering more MW lowers the probability of clearing at a good price, so expected revenue is concave in offered volume.
Capacity-curve concavity is verified against the breakpoints rather than assumed.
If the fitted capacity curve is not concave that is a modelling signal, and it must be declared General, costing binaries, rather than mis-declared.
AfrrEnergyView and ImbalanceRiskView emit LinearTerms for expected activation value and a convex minimising PwlTerm for the CVaR functional on imbalance cost.
CVaR is linear-programmable, so the risk term does not change the problem class.
CVaR is chosen over a variance penalty because it carries the same risk intent with no quadratic term and no loss of MILP structure.
Activation and imbalance draw from the same scenario axis as prices, which is what makes activation-when-prices-are-extreme representable at all.
IdOptionView emits a concave PwlTerm in volume, because the marginal MWh gets a worse price, plus BoundTerms from SOC and efficiency feasibility.
IdOptionView covers directional buy and sell, restricted to volumes the battery can physically support.
The intraday volume restriction is a bound rather than a penalty, because an infeasible intraday plan is not a cheap plan but an invalid one.

FillProbView emits BoundTerms only, and because no price field exists on a BoundTerm the intent of constraining volume without telling the Planner what the fill would earn is enforced by the type system rather than by convention.
The full fill-probability curve is available to the quoting policy through a separate path, which is where the price/probability trade-off belongs.
DelineationView prices the two delineation routes and the levies they relieve.
DelineationView emits LinearTerms carrying the marginal values λ_j of the seven month-to-date accumulators, plus BoundTerms bounding q to available generation.

DelineationView emits no coefficient on any lever, so curtailment, charge source, discharge routing and reserve headroom reach the objective only through the accumulator state equations the Planner carries.
A lever coefficient would have to embed a MIN-branch case analysis evaluated at a state not yet chosen.

V_del is evaluated arithmetically and never fitted, because given a projection of the remaining month every quantity from (10) to (33) is closed-form, so the λ_j are derivatives of published formulas.
There is no delineation artefact to go stale, only a projection to refresh.
V_del is evaluated per scenario and the tail of V_del itself is taken, not a per-accumulator sign.

Because MAX[AW − MW_month; 0] is convex the mean projection understates the premium, the direction of pessimism differs per accumulator, and a single cvarLevel would push some accumulators the wrong way.
Delineation curvature exists only through grid charging: at (9) = 0 the ratio in (31) = (30)·(28) cancels and the whole green route is a per-slot linear sum.

TariffView emits LinearTerms only, from a closed enumerated list of the volumetric network charge and the taxes and surcharges a delineation regime cannot reduce, all normalised to EUR/MWh and stamped for the tick.
The reducible EnFG components are not in TariffView but are charged on (21) by DelineationView at stage 3.
The closed tariff component list is enforced: the configuration enumerates permitted components and an unrecognised component is a configuration error rather than a silently ignored field.

A PvCurtailmentView is not needed and is deliberately absent, because q is a Planner decision variable bounded by DelineationView to available generation and priced against spot and the delineation λ_j.
A view that scheduled curtailment would be a rule wearing a price.
A SelfConsumptionView is not needed and is deliberately absent, because avoided import is already TariffView plus SpotView and the delineation leg falls out of the accumulator state equations.
The absence of a SelfConsumptionView should be revisited only if retail supply stops being spot-indexed.
A CapacityMarketView and redispatch are out of scope for v1.
Individual views do not give a usable objective because the terms interact.
The composer applies views in stages with declared preconditions, so that composing in the wrong order raises an exception rather than producing a plausible wrong number.
Composer stage 1, Tariff, requires nothing and establishes that POI energy is fully marked, because everything downstream prices marked energy.

Composer stage 2, OppCost plus V, requires POI energy marked and establishes battery energy marked with terminal value attached, because battery energy must carry its own cost before anything prices its use.

Composer stage 3, Delineation, requires battery energy marked and establishes (21) with the delineation λ attached, because levies are charged on (21) which depends on the month's PV-versus-grid charging mix and so cannot be marked at stage 1.
Composer stage 4, ReserveCoupling, requires battery energy marked and establishes the SOC corridor and headroom constraints, because reserve consumes headroom which must exist before peak prices it.

Composer stage 5, Peak, requires both POI and battery energy marked and establishes zPeak bounded below by the realised peak, because peak headroom is priced on top of a battery whose energy is already marked and reversing this double-counts.
Composer stage 6, Validate, requires all previous stages and establishes that the bundle is well-formed and complete.
The L2 stage table is the single source for stage order, and the invariant, the T2 section and the interface stubs point at it rather than restating it.
Stage 1 carries only the non-reducible tariff surface and stays linear.

The reducible EnFG components move to stage 3 because their base (21) is not knowable until battery energy is marked, which is the one place where the original tariff-then-oppcost-then-peak ordering could not be preserved.

The composer collects terms from every enabled view, then runs the ownership check, the stage precondition check, curvature verification, unit and range validation, risk profile assembly and the problem class hint, and finally seals the bundle by computing its contentHash.
The composer performs no economics: it never adds, scales or reconciles a term.
If two terms would overlap the composer fails rather than netting them, because netting would be economics and economics belongs in a view where it can be tested.
The term ownership matrix is normative and each effect has exactly one owner.
SpotEnergyValue is owned by SpotView on the MarketVolume base.
IdEnergyValue is owned by IdOptionView on the MarketVolume base.
ReserveCapacityRevenue is owned by AfrrCapacityView on the ReserveCapacity base.
ReserveEnergyRevenue is owned by AfrrEnergyView on the MarketVolume base.
ImbalanceCost is owned by ImbalanceRiskView on the MarketVolume base.
NetworkPeakCharge is owned by PeakView on the PoiImport base.
NetworkVolumetricCharge is owned by TariffView on the PoiImport base.
LeviesAndTaxes is owned by TariffView on the PoiImport base.
EnfgLevies is owned by DelineationView on the Delineation base.
SubsidyRevenue is owned by DelineationView on the Delineation base.
CycleDegradation is owned by OppCostView on the BatteryThroughput base.
StoredEnergyContinuation is owned by OppCostView via V on the TerminalSoc base.
ActivationRisk is owned by AfrrEnergyView on the MarketVolume base.
DA energy value enters as a LinearTerm on vDaBuy and vDaSell emitted by a thin SpotView.
SpotView is added deliberately, because leaving it implicit is how the largest term in the objective ends up owned by nobody.
Leaving SpotView implicit would violate both the origin-view invariant and the rule that the Planner adds no economics of its own.
SpotView is trivial to implement and its existence is what keeps the origin-view and no-Planner-economics rules true.
LeviesAndTaxes carries the components a delineation regime cannot reduce — Stromsteuer and Konzessionsabgabe — on PoiImport, while EnfgLevies carries the reducible EnFG components on (21).
The levy split is a base split and not relief booked as revenue, so exclusivity is unaffected and (20) is reported as a diagnostic quantity and never as an effect.
SubsidyRevenue is the Marktprämie MAX[AW − MW_month; 0] on (32) only.
Spot revenue on the same exported kWh stays in SpotEnergyValue, which makes the double count impossible by construction rather than by check.
Two effects may share a base, as NetworkPeakCharge and NetworkVolumetricCharge both do on PoiImport, and that is legitimate and common.
What is forbidden is two terms claiming the same effect on the same base and slot.
Quality never becomes a branch but becomes parameters.
Degraded load quality raises peakSafetyMarginKw and raises cvarLevel for peak.
Degraded pv quality raises peakSafetyMarginKw, because a PV shortfall raises import.
Degraded price beliefs lower positionScale and raise cvarWeight.
Degraded activation beliefs raise chanceLevel for SOC feasibility.
A stale V(SOC) has the stalenessPenalty shrink applied to its slopes.
Degraded liquidity beliefs lower the idReliableVolume bounds, which are already conservative at C1.
Every risk adjustment is recorded in riskProfile.driverSummary, so a conservative plan can always be explained by naming the input that caused it.
L2 determinism means the same C1 in gives byte-identical C2 out.
Schema closure means a view's output contains only declared fields.
Raising peakPrice never lowers the priced value of peak reduction, and raising afrrCapPrice never lowers the capacity curve.
A term whose price is zero contributes nothing.
Scaling all prices by k greater than zero scales all EUR terms by k and leaves all bounds unchanged.
Scale equivariance catches a surprising number of unit-mixing bugs in one cheap test.
V's slopes are strictly decreasing and the capacity curve is concave.
A view given a permuted scenario axis on one series only must produce a different output, and if it does not that view is ignoring the dependence structure ADR-005 exists to preserve.
